audit.whatIsWrong: content.early says "Ziggs's Bouncing Bomb simply reaches farther", whys[0] says Tongue Lash out-ranges "your auto but not his Bouncing Bomb", and spikes[0].text says "Ziggs's Bouncing Bomb outranges your Tongue Lash at level 1".
audit.why: On cast range it is the other way round. Tongue Lash is 900; Bouncing Bomb is 850. His extra reach comes entirely from the bomb bouncing twice past the landing point, which is a different thing to counterplay — you can stand at a distance where he cannot CAST on you but the bounces still arrive, and you can also step to 900 and win the range war outright if he has committed a bomb to the wave. Told flatly that he out-ranges you, the player never contests the level-1 poke at all and concedes a lane he can actually trade in.
audit.corrected: Tongue Lash 900 vs Bouncing Bomb 850 at the cast. The reach advantage is in the bounces, not the cast range.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ziggs.json and champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (Riot Data Dragon 16.15.1) — range fields

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1] says Satchel Charge "resets your An Acquired Taste progress mid-approach" and wants.foe[2] says to use it "resetting his An Acquired Taste progress before the stun lands".
audit.why: Nothing in Riot's text gives Satchel Charge any effect on An Acquired Taste. It knocks enemies away — that is all. The real reason to bait it is displacement: it removes you from the 900-range band you need to be in, and it does so on a 20/18/16/14/12s cooldown. Inventing a stack-reset makes the player think a landed Satchel undoes work that is in fact still banked, so he re-stacks from scratch instead of walking straight back in.
audit.corrected: Satchel Charge knocks you off the approach. It does not touch your stacks, and it is 20s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid, whys[4] and spikes[1].text build level 6 around "Abyssal Voyage" — "he now has to track your position globally", "you able to teleport behind him", "threaten a flank or TP-mirror play". content.late and spikes[3].text also refer to "your R to reappear from an unexpected vector" and being unable to reach him "without your R".
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is Tahm Kench's removed pre-2020 W. There is no global and no reappearing flank in the live kit — the W is Abyssal Dive at 1000-1200 range, and the R is Devour. Against a long-range mage this is the most damaging place for the error to sit, because the entire stated answer to being kited is a flank tool that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is Devour. The answer to Ziggs is banking three stacks and closing to 900, plus Teleport for the map game.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late says "If you land the three-stack stun and swallow him", and tldr/winCon/dosFull all say "stack-stun him on the Satchel Charge cooldown and Devour the kill". dosFull[2] is titled "Q-stun at 3 stacks when Satchel Charge is down".
audit.why: The stun and Devour are alternative spenders of the same three stacks — Riot's Q text says the stacks are consumed by the stun, and the passive requires three stacks to Devour. In this matchup the mistake is unusually costly: you get one approach through the minefield per Satchel cooldown, and spending it on a stun leaves you standing next to Ziggs with a greyed-out ultimate and no second window.
audit.corrected: Bank three stacks, close, and Devour. Never spend the stacks on a stun here.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (Riot Data Dragon 16.15.1) — P and Q descriptions

audit.whatIsWrong: Satchel Charge is correctly identified as matchup-defining in the full layer but never given a cooldown, and no range or cooldown for any Ziggs ability appears anywhere.
audit.why: This matchup is entirely a spacing problem, so the numbers ARE the advice: Tongue Lash 900, Bouncing Bomb 850 on 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s, Hexplosive Minefield 900 on a flat 16s, Satchel Charge 1000 on 20/18/16/14/12s, Mega Inferno Bomb 5000 on 120/95/70s. The 20-second Satchel window is the only reliable approach in the lane and the player is never told how long it lasts.
audit.corrected: Satchel Charge 20/18/16/14/12s at 1000 range is the window. Minefield flat 16s at 900.

audit.why: Its cooldown is REDUCED every time Ziggs casts an ability, so a Ziggs shoving the wave has his empowered auto up far more often than a passive one does. For a Tahm Kench deciding whether to hold position at the edge of poke range, that means the cost of standing there scales with how much he is casting — which is exactly the opposite of the usual read that a mage spending abilities on the wave is temporarily harmless.
audit.corrected: Short Fuse's cooldown drops with every ability cast, so his empowered auto comes back faster the more he bombs the wave.

edits.before: Tongue Lash has solid range but Ziggs's Bouncing Bomb simply reaches farther, and he can chip your grey health before you ever get near three An Acquired Taste stacks. At level 1 sit at max Tongue Lash distance, poke back whenever he steps up to bomb the wave, and let Thick Skin absorb what you cannot dodge — do not walk up to auto stack because the moment you step into his bomb arc you eat two bombs and a bounce for every one slow you land. At level 2 he gets Satchel Charge and your job changes: fake a walk-in to bait the Satchel Charge, then immediately Tongue Lash when the cooldown is burning — that is your only safe window to fish for a third stack without getting knocked back at the stun frame.
edits.after: Tongue Lash is cast at 900 and Bouncing Bomb at 850, so he does not out-range you at the cast — it is the two bounces past the landing point that give him the extra reach. At level 1 sit at max Tongue Lash distance, poke back whenever he steps up to bomb the wave, and let Thick Skin absorb what you cannot dodge — do not walk up to auto stack, because the moment you step into his bomb arc you eat two bombs and a bounce for every slow you land. Satchel Charge is his knockback and it is 20s at rank 1: fake a walk-in to bait it, then commit your Tongue Lash into that cooldown — that is your only safe window to fish for the third stack.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are the hardest stretch of this lane. Ziggs has Hexplosive Minefield now and can cut off every approach path while continuing to bomb the wave from behind it; without your R you cannot flank, and without a tank item your grey health converts too slowly to win an attrition war against sustained bomb poke. Park at the edge of minion range, last-hit with Tongue Lash, and accept that you are playing for CS not kills. Level 6 is a genuine turning point: Abyssal Voyage means he now has to track your position globally and cannot freely shove without wondering where you reappeared from. Use it to impact another lane and return with gold — a first-recall Heartsteel or Sunfire Aegis changes the math of the lane entirely.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are the hardest stretch of this lane. Ziggs has Hexplosive Minefield now — 900 range on a flat 16s — and can cut off every approach path while continuing to bomb the wave from behind it; without a tank item your grey health converts too slowly to win an attrition war against sustained bomb poke. Note that Short Fuse's cooldown drops every time he casts, so standing in poke range gets worse the more he bombs. Park at the edge of minion range, last-hit with Tongue Lash, and accept that you are playing for CS not kills. Level 6 is a genuine turning point, but not because of any global: Devour is a duel button, and a first-recall Heartsteel or Sunfire Aegis changes the math of the lane entirely.

edits.before: Once you have a tank item your grey-health engine starts winning the war of attrition: you can absorb two or three bomb volleys, walk through the minefield, and Tongue Lash into Devour removes him from a teamfight in a way he has almost no answer to once you bridge the distance. The key late-game ask is getting on top of him — Ziggs has Satchel Charge and good positioning so you need your team to create the angle or your R to reappear from an unexpected vector. If you land the three-stack stun and swallow him during a baron or dragon fight, Ziggs is simply out of the fight for three seconds with no way to bomb, and that is the entire win condition of this matchup scaled up.
edits.after: Once you have a tank item your grey-health engine starts winning the war of attrition: you can absorb two or three bomb volleys, walk through the minefield, and Devour removes him from a teamfight in a way he has almost no answer to once you bridge the distance. The key late-game ask is getting on top of him — Satchel Charge knocks you off from 1000 range on a 20s cooldown, so you need your team or the fog to create the angle. Bank three An Acquired Taste stacks BEFORE the fight and swallow him at baron or dragon: spend them on a stun instead and the ultimate is greyed out, which is this whole matchup in one mistake.

notes: FALSE INTERACTION IN THE SOURCE DATA — do not propagate: _missing-interactions.json lists "resistances-invalidated: Ziggs bypasses stacking resistances (Satchel Charge (W))" for this matchup, and zac.json/ziggs.json both carry a percentHealth flag on Satchel Charge. Riot's Satchel Charge text has no percent-health component at all; the flag looks derived from the clause about hexploding "vulnerable enemy turrets". I did not write anything based on it. Worth checking the flag-derivation rule, because a false "armour will not help you" line would push Tahm Kench players off the correct build. Separately, note the difficulty ratings are not calibrated to win rate anywhere in this file: Ziggs at 51.55% is HARD 8.5/10 while Yorick at 45.77% is EVEN 6/10. I left Ziggs alone (the lane genuinely plays awkwardly) but flagged Yorick in its own proposal.
